hook: SCP-3812 is long and builds slowly through an interview, memos, an event log and an essay, so give it a proper sitting. It leans on the idea that realities can be stacked like stories inside stories, but the article explains what it needs as it goes. Keep its subtitle, A Voice Behind Me, in mind the whole way through.
whyItMatters: The article is about authors, characters and the layers between them, and it turns that question into a containment problem. It builds on Foundation concepts that the memos explain on the spot, such as Dr. Scranton's reality anchors and the Hume as a measure of reality, then pushes them past the point where measurement means anything. Its event log also ties the entity to several other numbered items, so the file reaches well beyond its own pages.
thingsToNotice:
The file starts with a man, Sam Howell, who died in 1996 and climbed out of his grave, and in the 1999 interview he is frightened and apologetic, seeing more voices every day and saying that in the story the doctor does not try to help. The log then charts the damage of a mind that can no longer tell real from imagined: cars annihilated, an island and later Mongolia briefly erased, the whole world hearing him scream for help, and a concept, maybe an emotion, that has quietly ceased to exist. The Paraguay addendum, where tungsten rods, a sinkhole and a naked singularity all fail to touch him, reads as someone above the Foundation trying to delete a character.

The twist arrives in a note signed only B: the author of this universe built something that must supersede whatever supersedes it, and so it supersedes itself, now climbing past its own creator. Scranton's essay supplies the logic for that, and the climax delivers it. During an XK-class end of the world, with seas boiling away and SCP-610 and SCP-2932 breaking loose, two voices of the same entity argue, one seeking revenge on the writer named Ben, the other urging it to let go. They choose to leave, look down at a man at a keyboard waiting to see what they do, and the world is rewritten back as if nothing happened, which is where the subtitle finally pays off.

related.note: The event log says it was found in the crater left after a failed 2009 containment attempt.
The log reports that the remains of an anchor-like entity used against SCP-3812 were reclassified under this number.
A vanished record says SCP-3812 badly damaged it after its activation.
